mainTopic: Examining a miscarried embryo, שמואל's ruling on an embryo without hair, and the laws of a סנדל
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about examining a miscarried embryo: clean it with oil, not water, and look at it only in sunlight. The גמרא rereads the ברייתא's question 'כיצד בודקין אותו?' as asking how to tell male from female. אבא שאול gives a test with a smooth sliver of wood, and רב נחמן limits it to an upward motion. The גמרא adds a sign for a female embryo and describes how the forming arms and thighs look. Next it turns to שמואל's ruling: the woman must worry that she is טמאה, but she gets the ימי טהרה only if the embryo has hair. The גמרא explains that this doubt is meant for ordinary people, even though שמואל himself was an expert. Then it turns to the סנדל, a flattened fetus. It asks whether a סנדל needs a face shape, bringing שמואל, רבי יצחק and רבי ינאי. Finally it explains why the משנה needs to mention a סנדל at all, since one is always born with a twin, and it begins to look at another משנה that mentions a סנדל, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Examine the embryo with oil, and look only in sunlight
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its rule. Water harms the embryo, so it is examined with oil instead, which is soft and cleans it, and it is looked at only in sunlight.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Water is harsh] and breaks it apart. Rather, one examines it with oil, because oil is soft and cleans it. And one looks at it only in sunlight.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes explaining how to examine a miscarried embryo. It says to use oil, not water, and to look at it only in sunlight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water would break apart the delicate embryo, so the evidence would be lost. Oil is gentle and cleans it so the form can be seen clearly. Sunlight gives the best light for an accurate look.

phrases.english: and dissolves it.
phrases.notes: The start of this sentence comes just before: water is harsh, so it breaks the embryo apart.

phrases.english: Rather, one examines it with oil,
because oil is soft and cleans it,
and one looks at it only in sunlight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section about examining an embryo.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An embryo is examined with oil, not water, and viewed only in sunlight.

steps.title: Why ask how to examine it when we just said?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to ask 'כיצד בודקין אותו?' The גמרא is surprised, because the method was just explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'How does one examine it?' How does one examine it?! As we just said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next question in the ברייתא and objects to it. The method of examining was just given, so the question seems pointless. This sets up a new way to read the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא just finished explaining how to examine the embryo with oil and sunlight. Asking 'how do we examine it?' right afterward looks like a needless repeat. The גמרא assumes the ברייתא does not waste words, so the question must mean something else.
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'כיצד בודקין אותו?' is the ברייתא's own question. The second one, with the surprise, is the גמרא echoing it to show that it seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: How does one examine it?
How does one examine it?!
As we just said!
phrases.notes: He means the oil-and-sunlight method from the previous step.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ? כֵּיצַד בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ?! כִּדְאָמְרִינַן!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's next question because step 1 already answered it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'כיצד בודקין אותו' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The method of examination was just given, so asking it again would be a needless repeat.

steps.title: The question really asks how to tell male from female
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא's question: it is asking how to check whether the embryo is male or female.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: in what way does one examine it to know whether it is male or female?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own objection by reading the question differently. It is not asking how to clean and view the embryo. It is asking how to find out its gender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first examination with oil and sunlight showed whether the embryo is formed. Now there is a second question: is it a boy or a girl? This matters because the mother's days of טומאה and טהרה after birth depend on the baby's gender.

phrases.english: Rather, in what way does one examine it

phrases.aramaic: לֵידַע אִם זָכָר הוּא אִם נְקֵבָה הִיא?
phrases.english: to know whether it is male or whether it is female?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בַּמֶּה בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ לֵידַע אִם זָכָר הוּא אִם נְקֵבָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection in step 2 by reading the question as being about gender.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question seemed to repeat the request for the basic examination method.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question asks how to tell whether the embryo is male or female.

steps.title: אבא שאול's test with a smooth sliver of wood
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול says to move a smooth-tipped sliver over the private area. If it catches, the embryo is male. If not, it is female.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול בר נש, and some say אבא שאול בר רמש, says: One brings a sliver of wood with a smooth tip and moves it over that place. If it catches, it is known to be male. If not, it is known to be female.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the gender question with a physical test using a thin, smooth piece of wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A male organ, even a tiny one, would get in the way of the sliver and make it catch. If the sliver glides smoothly, there is no male organ, so the embryo is female. The smooth tip makes sure the wood itself does not cause the catching.

keyTerms.meaning: it is certain, it is known

phrases.english: Abba Shaul bar Nash,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אַבָּא שָׁאוּל בַּר רֶמֶשׂ, אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: and some say Abba Shaul bar Remash, says:
One brings a sliver of wood whose tip is smooth,
and moves it over that place.
phrases.notes: 'That place' is a polite way of saying the private area.

phrases.english: If it catches, it is known that it is male.
And if not, it is known that it is female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the gender question raised in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Move a smooth sliver over the area. If it catches, the embryo is male. If not, it is female.
steps.whatToRemember: The gender test: a smooth sliver that catches means male, and one that glides freely means female.

steps.title: The test only counts when the sliver moves from below to above
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, limits the test. Catching counts only when the sliver moves from bottom to top. Side-to-side catching might come from the walls of the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: They taught this only when the sliver moves from below to above. But if it moves from the sides, say that it caught on the walls of the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a limit to אבא שאול's test. Catching proves 'male' only when the sliver moves upward, not sideways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sliver moves sideways, it could catch on the side walls of the womb area, so catching would not prove a male organ. Moving from below to above avoids that problem, so a catch there points to a male. This narrows how the test must be done, without rejecting it.

keyTerms.meaning: they taught this only when, a limiting phrase

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a sign only proves something when no other explanation exists. If a catch could come from something else, it proves nothing.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
They taught this only when it moves from below to above,
phrases.notes: 'This' means אבא שאול's rule that catching shows the embryo is male.

phrases.english: but if it moves from the sides,
say that it is the walls of the womb.
phrases.notes: In other words, the sliver may have caught on the walls, not on a male organ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the gender test given in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A catch proves the embryo is male only when the sliver moves from below to above. A sideways catch may come from the walls of the womb.
steps.whatToRemember: The sliver test proves 'male' only with an upward motion. A sideways catch proves nothing.

steps.title: The sign of a female embryo
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה quotes a teaching: a female embryo shows a line like a split barley grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: It was taught: if the embryo was female, you can tell by a line that looks like a split barley grain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה adds the sign of a female embryo to the description of the embryo.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, we only had a test for a male: the sliver catches. Now we also have a positive sign for a female: a lengthwise line, like the crack running down a barley grain.

keyTerms.meaning: A split barley grain, which has a crack down its length

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: תָּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said: It was taught,
"If it was female,
it is identified like a split barley grain."
phrases.notes: He means the female private area looks like a thin line, like the crack running down a barley grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a sign for a female embryo to the male test of אבא שאול
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A female embryo is recognized by a line like a split barley grain.

steps.title: Maybe the line belongs to a male
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks whether the line might really be the seam between a male's testicles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן objected: But maybe that line is the seam between the testicles, and the embryo is really male?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges the female sign. He says the line could belong to a male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a male body also has a line in the same place, then seeing a line proves nothing. The sign would not separate male from female.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman objects to it:
But maybe it is the seam between the testicles?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the female sign from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The split-barley sign for a female
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A male also has a line-like seam, so the sign may be ambiguous.

steps.title: Too early to see the seam
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers: at this stage even the testicles cannot be seen, so their seam certainly cannot be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: At this stage, even the testicles themselves cannot be seen. Could the seam between them be seen?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the female sign against רב נחמן's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seam is a small detail of the testicles. If the testicles are not yet visible in such an early embryo, their seam cannot be visible either. So a visible line must be the female sign.

keyTerms.meaning: Now. It opens a 'how much more so' style argument

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Now, the testicles themselves are not noticeable,
so would the seam between the testicles be noticeable?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַשְׁתָּא בֵּיצִים גּוּפַיְיהוּ לָא יְדִיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual reality: the confusing feature does not exist yet at this stage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line might be a male's seam
steps.terutzMaskana: At this stage a male's seam cannot be seen, so the line is a female sign

steps.title: What the thighs and arms look like
steps.stepSummary: רבי עמרם quotes a teaching: the thighs and arms look like red threads. The thighs are like the thicker ערב threads, and the arms are like the thinner שתי threads.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עמרם said: It was taught: its two thighs are like two red threads. רבי עמרם added: like ערב threads. Its two arms are like two red threads. רבי עמרם added: like שתי threads.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עמרם describes how the limbs look when they first begin to form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching compares both thighs and arms to red threads. רבי עמרם adds which kind of thread each one is like. The thighs are like the thicker ערב threads, and the arms are like the thinner שתי threads.

phrases.english: Rabbi Amram said, it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי יַרְכוֹתָיו כִּשְׁנֵי חוּטִין שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית.
phrases.english: Its two thighs are like two threads of red wool.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי עַמְרָם עֲלַהּ: כְּשֶׁל עֵרֶב.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Amram said about it: like threads of the woof.
phrases.notes: In weaving, the ערב threads are thicker than the שתי threads, so the thighs are thicker than the arms.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁנֵי זְרוֹעוֹתָיו כִּשְׁנֵי חוּטִין שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית,
phrases.english: And its two arms are like two threads of red wool,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי עַמְרָם עֲלַהּ: כְּשֶׁל שְׁתִי.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Amram said about it: like threads of the warp.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עַמְרָם, תָּנָא: שְׁתֵּי יַרְכוֹתָיו כִּשְׁנֵי חוּטִין שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the signs of male and female to the look of the limbs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The forming thighs look like thick red threads, and the arms look like thinner red threads.

steps.title: Do not rule until there is hair
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב יהודה not to rule in practice about such an embryo until it has grown hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: Sharp one, do not act on this in practice until the embryo has grown hair.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a practical limit: do not treat such an early embryo as a real birth until it has hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the descriptions so far tell us what an early embryo looks like. שמואל says that in practice, we should not rule on a woman as having given birth until the embryo has hair.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharp one. שמואל's nickname for רב יהודה

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
Sharp one,
phrases.notes: This is a friendly nickname שמואל used for his student רב יהודה.

phrases.english: do not act on it in practice until it grows hair.
phrases.notes: He means: don't rule that she is טמאה as one who gave birth until the embryo has hair.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה: שִׁינָּנָא, לָא תַּעֲבֵיד עוֹבָדָא עַד שֶׁיַּשְׂעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from describing the embryo to how to rule in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not rule in practice that this is a birth until the embryo has hair.

steps.title: שמואל seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's rule from another ruling of his: in both cases the woman must be concerned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did שמואל really say this? But שמואל said: in both this case and that case, she must be concerned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that שמואל's rule seems to clash with another ruling he gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In another case שמואל said that a woman who passed a sac must worry that it was a real birth, even without any hair. That seems to contradict his rule here: 'do not rule until there is hair.'

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? A formula that challenges a statement from the same person's other words
Both this case and that case
She must be concerned (that it may have been a birth)

phrases.english: But did Shmuel really say this?
But Shmuel said:
Both in this case and in that case, she must be concerned!
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's ruling about a woman who passed a sac, whether its fluid was cloudy or clear.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10 using another ruling of שמואל
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule not to rule until there is hair
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere שמואל requires concern even without hair, which looks like a contradiction.

steps.title: Concern, yes; ימי טהרה, no
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי בר שמואל explains that שמואל told him: she must be concerned that she is טמאה, but she does not get the ימי טהרה until the embryo has hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי בר שמואל said: מר שמואל explained it to me himself. As for being concerned, she must be concerned. But we do not give her the ימי טהרה unless the embryo has grown hair.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אמי בר שמואל settles the contradiction by quoting שמואל's own explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rulings are about different things. Out of doubt, she must keep the stricter side and worry that she is טמאה as one who gave birth. But the leniency of ימי טהרה, when blood she sees is treated as pure, is given only once the embryo has hair.

keyTerms.meaning: To be concerned, to act strictly out of doubt
The days after birth when blood a woman sees is treated as pure

steps.whatToRemember: An embryo without hair: the woman acts strictly and worries that she is טמאה as one who gave birth. But she gets the lenient ימי טהרה only if the embryo has hair.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Do not act until there is hair' does not mean she is completely free. It only means we do not give her the lenient ימי טהרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: when we are in doubt, we take the strict side and do not apply the leniency.

phrases.english: Rav Ami bar Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל —
phrases.english: To me it was explained by Mar Shmuel himself:
as for being concerned, she is concerned;
but the days of purity we do not give her
phrases.notes: After the days of impurity that follow a birth comes a period when blood she sees is pure. These are those days.

phrases.english: until it has grown hair.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַמֵּי בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ruling: strict concern versus the lenient ימי טהרה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's two rulings contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: She must be concerned that she is טמאה, but she gets ימי טהרה only once the embryo has hair

steps.title: How could the expert שמואל be unsure about an embryo?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that שמואל was in doubt about an early embryo. It points to a story where he dated a שפיר to exactly 41 days and caught a husband who had been with his wife while she was a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean שמואל was unsure? But a certain שפיר was brought before שמואל. He said, 'This one is 41 days old.' He counted from the day the woman went to טבילה until that day, and it was only 40 days. He said, 'This husband was with her while she was a נדה.' They tied the husband up, and he admitted it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea from the last step that שמואל was in doubt. It tells a story showing that he could read an embryo's age down to the exact day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12, שמואל said she must worry about טומאה but does not get the ימי טהרה, which shows he was in doubt. But if he could tell that an embryo was 41 days old, and not 40, he clearly knew embryos perfectly. So how could he ever be unsure?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say?' A word that opens a challenge to a conclusion
A gestational sac, an embryo still in its sac
Immersion in a מקוה, which ends a woman's נדה state
A woman in her menstrual state, when relations are forbidden

phrases.english: Is that to say that שמואל is unsure?
But there was a certain gestational sac
that was brought before מר שמואל,
he said: 'This one is forty-one days old,'
and he counted from the day she went to immerse
until that day,
and it was only forty days,
phrases.notes: So the baby was started one day before she went to the מקוה, while she was still a נדה.

phrases.english: and he said to them: This man was with her while she was a נדה;
they tied him up, and he admitted it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the doubt behind שמואל's ruling in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that שמואל was unsure about the status of an early embryo
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who can date an embryo to the exact day cannot be unsure what it is

steps.title: שמואל was unusually skilled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל personally was different because his expertise was great. His doubtful ruling is meant for people who do not have his level of skill.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל is different, because his strength was great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שמואל himself could tell, but most people cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in step 12 was a general rule for everyone. Since most judges cannot read an embryo the way שמואל could, the rule treats it as a doubt. שמואל's own special skill does not change the rule for everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is different.' A word used to set one case apart from another
'His strength was great.' He had exceptional skill

phrases.english: שמואל is different,
because his strength was great.
phrases.notes: He means שמואל's skill in this area was far above everyone else's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the expert himself versus the general public
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's skill shows that there is no real doubt about early embryos
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubt in the ruling applies to ordinary people. שמואל personally could tell.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's doubtful ruling is a general rule for people without his rare skill. It does not mean he himself did not know.

steps.title: What a סנדל looks like
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's case of a woman who miscarries a סנדל. A ברייתא gives two descriptions: like a sea fish, or like the tongue of a large ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A woman who miscarries a סנדל, etc.' The רבנן taught: A סנדל looks like a sea fish. At first it was a real baby, but it got flattened. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A סנדל looks like the tongue of a large ox.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about a סנדל and brings a ברייתא that describes what one looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view says the סנדל started out as a normal baby and was later squashed flat, so it looks like a flat fish. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a different picture: a large ox's tongue. Both views are trying to describe the shape so that people can recognize it.

keyTerms.meaning: A flattened fetus, named after a flat fish (or a sandal)

phrases.english: A woman who miscarries a סנדל, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, which says she keeps the rules of having given birth to both a boy and a girl.

phrases.english: The רבנן taught:
A סנדל looks like a fish of the sea,
from the start it was a baby,
but it was flattened.
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:

phrases.aramaic: סַנְדָּל דּוֹמֶה לַלָּשׁוֹן שֶׁל שׁוֹר הַגָּדוֹל.
phrases.english: A סנדל looks like the tongue of the large ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סנדל is a baby that was flattened, and it looks like a flat sea fish or an ox's tongue

steps.title: A סנדל needs the shape of a face
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא records a testimony in the name of earlier teachers: a סנדל only counts as a baby if it has a face shape.
steps.simpleTranslation: They testified in the name of our teachers: A סנדל needs the shape of a face.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a rule: for a סנדל to count as a real baby, it must have the form of a face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the ברייתא only described what a סנדל looks like. This testimony adds a real condition. Without a face shape, the flat mass does not get the status of a ולד.

keyTerms.meaning: They testified, passing on a teaching they had received
The shape or form of a face

phrases.english: They testified in the name of our teachers:
A סנדל needs the shape of a face.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a legal condition to the description in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סנדל counts as a ולד only if it has a face shape

steps.title: שמואל rules that the testimony is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows the testimony that a סנדל needs a face shape.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is that a סנדל needs the shape of a face.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל decides the practical law. We follow the testimony from step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא can record a rule without telling us whether it is the final law. שמואל settles it: in practice, a סנדל with no face shape is not treated as a baby.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that שמואל said:
The הלכה is: a סנדל needs the shape of a face.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules in practice that the testimony of step 16 is the law
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, a סנדל needs a face shape to count as a ולד

steps.title: The face may even be on the back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says a סנדל needs a face shape, but the face can even be on its back. He compares it to a person who was slapped so hard that his face was turned around.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא said in the name of רב יוסף, in the name of רבי יצחק: A סנדל needs the shape of a face, even if it is on its back. It is like a person who slapped his friend and turned his face around to the back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק adds a detail to the face rule. The face does not have to be in the normal place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a סנדל was squashed, its face may have been pushed out of place. The parable explains this: just as a hard slap can twist a face backward, the pressure on the fetus can move its face to the back. As long as a face shape exists somewhere, it counts.
steps.whatToRemember: A סנדל counts as a baby only if it has a face shape, and the face counts even if it was pushed around to the back.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: רב אדא said that רב יוסף said that רבי יצחק said:
A סנדל needs the shape of a face,
and even if it is on its back.
It is like a person who slapped his friend,
and turned his face around to the back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the face rule: the face does not have to be in its normal place
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A face shape anywhere, even on the back, is enough for a סנדל to count as a ולד

steps.title: רבי ינאי objects to declaring a faceless סנדל טהור
steps.stepSummary: In רבי ינאי's time, Sages wanted to rule that a סנדל without a face shape does not make the mother טמאה. רבי ינאי protested that they were declaring real babies טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the days of רבי ינאי, they wanted to declare a סנדל with no face shape טהור. רבי ינאי told them: You have declared babies טהור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that רבי ינאי holds a סנדל counts as a baby even without a face shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 brought a testimony that a סנדל needs a face shape. רבי ינאי disagrees. To him, ruling a faceless סנדל טהור means ignoring a real birth, so the mother would wrongly escape the טומאה of a woman who gave birth.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat, misshapen fetus that looks like a sandal-shaped fish

phrases.english: In the days of Rabbi Yannai,
they wanted to declare the sandal-fetus pure
phrases.notes: He means the mother who miscarried it would not become טמאה like a woman who gave birth.

phrases.english: that does not have the shape of a face.
Rabbi Yannai said to them:
You have declared babies pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a view that disagrees with the face-shape requirement of steps 16-18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ינאי, a סנדל without a face shape still counts as a baby and makes the mother טמאה.

steps.title: Challenge from the testimony that a סנדל needs a face
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ינאי from the ברייתא's testimony that a סנדל needs a face shape.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: In the name of our teachers they testified that a סנדל needs a face shape!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי ינאי's position using the testimony quoted earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא records a testimony from earlier teachers that a סנדל counts only with a face shape. That seems to support the Sages who wanted to declare it טהור, against רבי ינאי.

keyTerms.meaning: They testified (passed on an accepted ruling)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
In the name of our teachers they testified:
phrases.notes: This is the same testimony from step 16.

phrases.english: A sandal-fetus needs the shape of a face!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ינאי's ruling in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's claim that a faceless סנדל is a baby
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא records an accepted testimony that a סנדל needs a face shape, which contradicts רבי ינאי.

steps.title: The testimony is only רבי נחוניא's view
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי, quoting רבי יוחנן, answers that the testimony comes from רבי נחוניא alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This teaching was taught from the testimony of רבי נחוניא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי ינאי by saying the testimony is just one sage's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The testimony sounded like an accepted rule. Now we learn it comes from רבי נחוניא alone. So רבי ינאי can disagree with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony, a ruling passed on by a witness

steps.confusionAlert: Step 17 said שמואל rules like the testimony. This step does not erase that. It explains how רבי ינאי (and רבי יוחנן's tradition) could disagree.

phrases.english: Rav Bivi bar Abaye said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
From the testimony of Rabbi Nechunya
this teaching was taught.
phrases.notes: He means it is one sage's view, not a rule everyone must follow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the authority of the source: it is an individual's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The testimony is an accepted rule that רבי ינאי cannot argue with.
steps.terutzMaskana: The testimony is only רבי נחוניא's view, so רבי ינאי may disagree.

steps.title: רב ביבי earned credit by speaking first
steps.stepSummary: רבי זעירא says he and רב ביבי both heard this from רבי יוחנן, but רב ביבי said it first and got the credit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זעירא said: רב ביבי earned this teaching in his name. He and I were sitting before רבי יוחנן when he said it, but רב ביבי said it over first and earned the credit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side remark about who gets credit for the teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זעירא heard the same words from רבי יוחנן. But since רב ביבי repeated it first, the teaching is quoted in his name. This does not change the הלכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Rav Bivi earned credit for this teaching,
for he and I were sitting
before Rabbi Yochanan
when he said this teaching,
and he went first and said it over
and earned credit for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא: זְכָה בַּהּ רַב בִּיבִי בִּשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side remark about the teaching in step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The teaching is quoted in רב ביבי's name because he said it over first.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to mention a סנדל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה bothers with a סנדל, since a סנדל always comes with another baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they mention a סנדל? Isn't it true that there is no סנדל without another baby with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the משנה and asks why its סנדל ruling is needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סנדל is always born with another baby. That other baby already makes the mother a יולדת. So the סנדל seems to add nothing.

phrases.english: Why did they mention a sandal-fetus,
phrases.notes: The משנה said a woman who miscarries a סנדל keeps the rules for both a boy and a girl.

phrases.english: isn't it true that there is no sandal-fetus
that doesn't have a baby with it?
phrases.notes: So the mother is already a יולדת because of the other baby.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the face-shape debate and returns to the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling about a סנדל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since another baby always comes with a סנדל, the mother is a יולדת anyway, so the ruling seems pointless.

steps.title: The ruling matters when the other baby is a boy
steps.stepSummary: If the other baby is a girl, the סנדל adds nothing. But the משנה is talking about a case where the other baby is a boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a girl was born with it, that is true. But here we are dealing with a case where a boy was born with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the משנה to a case where the סנדל ruling makes a difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl already gives the mother the stricter rules of a girl, so the סנדל changes nothing. With a boy, the mother would only keep a boy's rules. Because the סנדל might be a girl, it adds the girl's rules too.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with?

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's סנדל ruling matters when the twin is a boy. The סנדל adds the stricter rules of a girl.

phrases.english: If a girl was born with it,
indeed, so it is,
phrases.notes: Meaning: you're right, in that case the סנדל adds nothing.

phrases.english: here, what case are we dealing with?
Where a boy was born with it.
phrases.notes: With only a boy, she'd keep a boy's shorter rules. The סנדל adds a girl's stricter ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּאִתְיְלִידָא נְקֵבָה בַּהֲדֵיהּ הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case (הכא במאי עסקינן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סנדל ruling never adds anything because another baby is always there.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the other baby is a boy, the סנדל adds the stricter rules of a girl.

steps.title: You might think a boy twin means the סנדל is a boy too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the mistaken assumption the משנה wants to stop: since gender depends on who emits seed first, a boy twin might seem to prove the סנדל is also a boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רב יצחק בר אמי taught that if the woman emits seed first, the baby is a boy, and if the man emits seed first, the baby is a girl. So since this twin is a boy, the סנדל must also be a boy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the answer from Step 24 by showing the wrong idea someone could have had. This sets up the next line, where the גמרא says what the משנה actually teaches us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק בר אמי says a baby's gender depends on who emits seed first at conception. Twins come from one act of conception, so you might think both babies must be the same gender. If that were true, a boy twin would mean the סנדל is surely a boy, and the mother would only need to keep the rules for a boy.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. It introduces a mistaken idea the text wants to reject.
Emits seed, at the moment of conception

steps.confusionAlert: This line is NOT the conclusion. It is the wrong idea (the הוה אמינא) that the next line, קא משמע לן, rejects.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: since Rav Yitzchak bar Ami said,
if the woman emits seed first, she gives birth to a male;
if the man emits seed first, she gives birth to a female;
so from the fact that this one is male, that one is also male.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the normal twin, and "that one" is the סנדל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind Step 24's answer by laying out the wrong idea the משנה wants to stop.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a הוה אמינא that makes the משנה's statement needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Twins share one conception, so a boy twin proves the סנדל is a boy as well.

steps.title: Both may have emitted seed together, so the twins can differ
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a boy twin proves nothing, because both parents may have emitted seed at the same time, making one twin a boy and the other a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches us that we can say both parents emitted seed at the same moment, so this twin is a boy and the סנדל is a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes Step 24's answer. The משנה needs to say the mother keeps the girl rules too, because the סנדל might be a girl even though its twin is a boy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק בר אמי's rule only covers cases where one parent is clearly first. If both emitted seed at once, one twin could be a boy and the other a girl. So the boy twin cannot prove the סנדל's gender, and the mother must keep the stricter rules of both.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us. This gives the real point after a mistaken idea.

steps.whatToRemember: Even when the סנדל's twin is a boy, the mother keeps the rules of a girl too, because the twins may be different genders.

phrases.english: It teaches us:
say that both emitted seed at the same time,
so this one is male and that one is female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the wrong idea from Step 25 and finishes the first answer to Step 23's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the הוה אמינא with a new possibility
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A boy twin proves the סנדל is a boy.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both parents may have emitted seed together, so the סנדל could be a girl, and the mother must keep the girl rules too.

steps.title: Second answer: births on two sides of sunset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another answer: the משנה's rule matters even when the twin is a girl, if the girl is born before sunset and the סנדל after sunset, because the start of her נדה count then depends on the סנדל's gender.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another answer: if she gives birth to the girl before sunset and to the סנדל after sunset, then she counts the start of her נדה period from the first birth or from the last birth, depending on the סנדל's gender.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to answer Step 23's question. Even with a girl twin, the סנדל's gender can matter when the two births fall on different days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After sunset counts as the next day, so the סנדל is born one day after the girl. If the סנדל is a boy, the girl's 80 days, counted from the first birth, are longer than his days, so she counts from the first birth. If the סנדל is a girl, her own 80 days run one day later, so she counts from the last birth. Because we are unsure, the mother must be strict both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunset, when a new day begins in הלכה
The day she goes back to regular נדה rules, once her birth periods are over
A flat, unformed fetus born together with a normal baby

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain why the משנה needs its rule about a סנדל: (1) a boy twin does not prove the סנדל is a boy; (2) even with a girl twin, births on two different days make the סנדל's gender matter.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a one-day gap between births can change when the woman's regular נדה status begins.

phrases.english: Another answer:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם תֵּלֵד נְקֵבָה לִפְנֵי שְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה,
phrases.english: for if she gives birth to the female before sunset,
and to the סנדל after sunset,
phrases.notes: After sunset counts as the next day, so the סנדל is born a day later.

phrases.english: she counts the start of נדה from the first,
and the start of נדה from the last.
phrases.notes: This is either one or the other: from the first birth if the סנדל is a boy, from the last if it is a girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, separate answer to Step 23's question, this time even when the twin is a girl.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative case where the סנדל's gender changes the outcome
steps.terutzMaskana: When the births are on different days, the סנדל's gender decides from which birth the start of נדה is counted, so the משנה's rule matters even with a girl twin.

steps.title: Turning to another משנה that mentions a סנדל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a different משנה that also speaks about a סנדל. It is getting ready to ask why that משנה needs to mention it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The סנדל that we learned about in a משנה...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא names another משנה that talks about a סנדל, and its next move will be to ask why that משנה needs this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before this explained why our משנה mentions a סנדל. Here the גמרא brings up another משנה with a סנדל case. Since a סנדל always comes with a twin, it will ask the same question about that משנה too.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat, sandal-shaped miscarried fetus. The גמרא says it is always born together with a twin.

phrases.english: A sandal [fetus], which we learned [in a mishna]

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the answers about our משנה (steps 24 to 27) and opens the same question about another משנה that mentions a סנדל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only introduces another משנה about a סנדל for the coming question.
